messages:
maya: heads-up — Topaz (int4) canary is spiking on funcall/structured-output parse errors for the knowledge_lookup tool. sample window 4k requests, parse_fail_rate from 0.5% -> 3.8% after the int4 rollout. putting raws and hypothesis here.
sam: link to the canary panel? want distribution by prompt length and route.
maya: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/topaz-canary -> query `funcall_parse_fail_rate{model=\"topaz-int4\"}`. top failing route: /agent/knowledge_lookup, then /agent/condense. failures skew to multi-line args and code-like snippets.
maya: examples below (raw outputs):
```
{"tool":"knowledge_lookup","args": {"query":"How to integrate Redwood API with streaming websockets?"}}}
{"tool":"knowledge_lookup","args": {"query":"How to integrate Redwood API with streaming websockets?",},}
{"tool":"knowledge_lookup","args":"query=How to integrate Redwood API with streaming websockets?"}...@@TRAILER@@
```
taylor: that looks like trailing-suffix and trailing-comma noise. any recent tokenizer/kernel diffs for topaz int4?
maya: build diff: quant kernel change to reduce memory copy; no intentional EOS semantics change. but that kernel includes a new packed-int4 codepath.
lee: can you reproduce locally? run tokenizer dump int8 vs int4 and include kvcache toggles.
sam: command I used to repro: `./tools/repro --model topaz --quant int4 --route /agent/knowledge_lookup --n 2500 --dump-token-ids --kvcache on`
canary-bot: ALERT: Topaz-canary cohort threshold breached (parse_fail_rate 3.8% > 1.8%). INC-2026-911 created.
taylor: quick repro results: int8 parse_fail 0.6% vs int4 3.7% with kvcache on. int4 + kvcache off -> 1.0%. token dumps show extraneous token sequence (id ~502) appended around EOS in many cases.
maya: good signal. two-pronged approach: (A) short-term tolerant postprocess 'struct-healer' that strips trailing non-json and fixes trailing commas; label healed outputs so we can measure impact and regressions; (B) kernel triage for packed-int4 kvcache interaction.
sam: agree. also run structured-eval (golden call set) comparing topaz-int8 vs topaz-int4 for schema-pass rate and semantic fidelity. queue 8k examples.
lee: will toggle canary config: disable kvcache for int4 cohort and reduce batch_size for streaming to 1 as a precaution.
taylor: I'll prototype the healer: on parse_error attempt: 1) remove trailing non-brace tokens after last closing brace, 2) strip trailing commas in objects/arrays, 3) reparse with up to 2 attempts. emit metric `struct_healer_applied` and `struct_healer_success`. label response with metadata `heuristic_healed=true`.
maya: ensure healer records original_text and healed_text hashes (not raw content) to check for semantic drift. we don't want heuristics to hide a real model regression.
sam: repro-run results after kvcache off + healer enabled (first 1.5k requests): raw parse_fail 3.7% -> post-healer 1.6% (healer fixed ~57% of failures). with kvcache off baseline down to ~0.9%.
taylor: good short-term. please don't auto-promote this as default behavior; add a canary-only flag.
lee: updating canary config: cohort B now has kvcache disabled and streaming batch_size=1. routing paused for further rollout.
canary-bot: NOTE: healer deployed to cohort B at 1815554388. monitoring healer metrics.
maya: created triage ticket ONB-1007: "topaz-int4 packed-kvcache EOS alignment" with token dumps attached.
sam: I'll kick off the structured-eval job (8k) now and post results when ready — measuring schema-strict pass, partial-parse, and semantic-similarity drift.
taylor: add a dashboard card to track fraction of healed responses that change semantics (compare embedding-sim between original and healed).
maya: agreed. pausing int4 rollout until kernel fix validated. we'll review structured-eval and kernel triage in tomorrow's stand. thanks all.
